meta.deadline_note: Hard cutoff Dec 31 — or whenever you hit it first.
meta.gap: ~+6–8" running vertical to control a ball over a 10-ft rim
meta.drivers: Vertical = max strength × reactive power × jump technique × power-to-weight. This block trains all four — plus mile/5K speed and an upper-body rebuild, all with no endurance interference.
meta.note: The off-season after Napa: endurance volume drops, which frees recovery for power + muscle. Running alone covers the cardio base — no bike or swim this block.
meta.cardio: 2–3 runs/week (~15–20 mi) fully maintains your aerobic base — and one is your speed session, so cardio and the mile/5K goal are the same runs.
meta.trip: India & Vietnam Nov 15 – Dec 6: equipment-light (bodyweight power + upper + running) and a planned diet break — eat the food.

progression: 1 · Foundation (low intensity): pogo hops, ankle hops, line hops, rope skipping — build tendon stiffness first.
2 · Eccentric control: slow step-downs (already doing) + low box step-offs, stick the landing — learn to absorb force.
3 · Bilateral jumps: countermovement jumps, box jumps (jump UP = soft landing), broad jumps.
4 · Unilateral: single-leg box jumps, short bounds.
5 · Reactive (HIGH intensity — knee must be bulletproof first): depth jumps, repeated hops, approach jumps.
Rule: advance a stage only when fully pain-free. Low volume, high intent, land soft, full recovery. Knee talks → drop back a stage.
technique: One-foot vs two-foot: test both. Most leapers jump higher off ONE foot with a running approach (more elastic); some are two-foot dominant.
Penultimate step: a long, low second-to-last step converts horizontal speed into vertical lift — the biggest technique lever.
Arm swing: a big double-arm (two-foot) or hard opposite-arm drive (one-foot) adds real inches. Time it with the jump.
Approach: 3–5 controlled, accelerating steps. Practice the rhythm, not just max effort.
Practice the full movement — approach + jump + reach — not just standing jumps.
testing: Standing reach: flat-footed, one arm fully up against a wall — mark it.
Max touch: jump and mark the highest point you touch (test both one- and two-foot).
Vertical = max touch − standing reach. Track monthly.
Targets: rim = 120". To control a ball over it, aim to touch ~126" (rim + ~6" clearance).
Re-test the 1st of each month — watch the gap to 126" shrink.

guide.cardio: You don't want to lose your aerobic base, but you don't need the bike or swim to keep it. 2–3 runs a week (~15–20 mi) fully maintains the engine coming off a 70.3 — and one of those is your mile/5K speed session, so cardio maintenance and getting faster are literally the same runs. Your swim is your strength (2nd AG at Napa) — it detrains slowly and comes back fast, and the bike rebuilds quickly in the IM block. Park both guilt-free this block.
guide.speed: The quality run each week is your mile/5K driver — rotate it: short reps (6×200m @ mile effort) and longer reps (5×300m @ mile–5K) for top-end; hill sprints and fartlek when legs are flat or you're travelling; a 1-mile time trial every 3–4 weeks as a benchmark (fresh legs only). Warm up 12–15 min and keep the hard running off legs that are trashed from lifting or plyo.
guide.upper: The off-season is the ideal window to rebuild upper body — endurance volume is low, so you have the recovery to build. Because you're regaining lost muscle (not building new), it comes back fast even in a slight deficit. Two push + two pull exposures a week (Tue/Thu at home; bodyweight on the trip) with progressive load. On the trip, bodyweight holds it well — push-up variations, dips, pull-ups, pike/handstand push-ups keep real volume; you only pause heavy barbell work.
guide.vertical: Your vertical is built from four things: raw max strength (heavy squats), reactive/elastic power (plyometrics — how fast you apply that strength), jump technique (approach + arm swing), and power-to-weight (getting lean). The base phase builds strength + technique + tendon base; the peak phase expresses reactive power and cuts the weight. Jumps and plyo are always done FRESH — never after heavy lifts or hard runs.
guide.ballcontrol: Getting your hand high enough is half the battle; controlling the ball over the rim is the other half. Palming a full basketball depends on hand size — if you can't, use a slightly under-inflated ball, a smaller ball, or a two-hand dunk. Decide with your friend what counts for the bet, and practice the actual finish, not just rim touches.
guide.knee: This is the goal where your PFPS history matters most — plyometrics are the exact eccentric-impact load that flared the knee. Follow the progression ladder strictly, keep the eccentric step-downs in daily as insurance, and never skip stages. If the knee objects, plyo comes out before anything else. A dunk isn't worth re-breaking the knee that carries every other goal.
guide.nutrition: Get lean with a gentle ~0.5 lb/wk cut (~300–500 kcal deficit) — power-to-weight is one of the fastest ways to add relative vertical, and the same lean-out reveals the abs (goal #3). Keep protein high (~1 g/lb, ~150–160g) so you hold muscle and power. Cycle it: fuel training days closer to maintenance, take the deficit on easy/rest days. The trip (Nov 15–Dec 6) is a planned diet break — eat at maintenance and enjoy it, then resume the cut Dec 7. Let performance govern: if lifts or jumps drop, ease the deficit.

gym.note: Base phase (home): 4 lifting days — Lower A (Mon), Upper Push (Tue), Upper Pull (Thu), Lower B (Fri) — plus plyo on the lower days, fresh. Trip: bodyweight power + upper. Peak phase: heavy-but-brief lower + reactive plyo + a power day + light upper maintenance, all on fresh legs.
